references.text: Jesus' answer in John 5:36 points directly to the same argument: that God's works (the miracles) testify about him, just as in 10:25 where he says that 'the works... testify about me'.

In John 8:18 Jesus uses the same logic regarding witnesses: 'I am the one who testifies about myself, and the Father... testifies about me', which corresponds with 10:25 where the Father's name and works testify.

John 12:37 summarizes the same conflict as in 10:25: 'Even though he had performed so many signs before them, they did not believe in him', which mirrors Jesus' complaint: 'I have told you this, and yet you do not believe'.

In John 15:24 Jesus repeats exactly the same point: 'If I had not done among them the works that no one else has done, they would not be guilty of sin; but now they have seen and hated both me and my Father', which links works directly to faith and testimony.

John 14:11 contains a direct parallel to 10:25 where Jesus asks people to believe because of the works: 'Believe me when I say that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; or at least believe on account of the works'.

In the same chapter, 10:37-38, Jesus expands the argument: 'If I do not do my Father's works, do not believe me; but if I do them, even though you do not believe me, believe the works', which is a direct extension of the statement in 10:25.
